key_insight: The paper reformulates SLBM into a predictor-corrector scheme that removes modified-equation errors while keeping the method simple and more stable for incompressible flows.
engineering_relevance: This improves accuracy, dissipation/dispersion control, and robustness for high-Reynolds-number CFD on relatively coarse grids.
method: Generalized SLBM formulation exposes intrinsic deviations and truncation errors in the macroscopic equations.
Predictor step uses tunable high-order SLBM parameters to control numerical dissipation and dispersion.
Corrector step applies finite-difference discretization of the BGK-LBM reference macroscopic equation.
evidence_signal: The approach is supported by linear wave analysis and numerical examples showing preserved second-order accuracy, better dissipation/dispersion behavior, and improved stability.
watch_item: Performance depends on choosing the tunable high-order parameters correctly, so implementation may require careful calibration across flow regimes.
paper_title: Revisit the simplified lattice Boltzmann method: dissipation, dispersion and stability
